# Auto Ontology [![#1 on the BEAVER leaderboard](https://img.shields.io/badge/BEAVER_leaderboard-%231-76b900)](https://beaverbench.github.io/#leaderboard) [![#2 on the BIRD-Interact leaderboard](https://img.shields.io/badge/BIRD--Interact_leaderboard-%232-76b900)](https://bird-interact.github.io/) Agents can retrieve documents and query databases, but reliability gates agentic analytics: a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong. Agents need context to answer accurately: what each business concept means, where it lives, how it connects, how to calculate it, where it comes from, and whether to trust it. An ontology holds that context: a shared, governed map from the concepts people ask about to the data behind them. NVIDIA Auto Ontology is an open library that builds that ontology automatically from enterprise metadata, reconciles definitions across systems, and exposes it to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. It complements the semantic models customers already own, and [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/) keeps it portable. It enables developers to: - **Discover:** generate enterprise ontologies from metadata; connect existing ontologies and semantic models; build AI-ready knowledge graphs. - **Ground:** give agents trusted business meaning for metrics, entities, and relationships; reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems. - **Validate:** test a draft with real questions before experts certify it; check generated queries against the catalog and the definitions retrieval surfaced; return the SQL and steps with every answer. - **Expose:** serve context to any agent harness through MCP, CLI, and API. - **Learn:** fold certified corrections and usage back into the ontology, so shared context improves with use. An ontology matters most when: - questions are varied, open-ended, and ambiguous; - data spans many disparate sources with overlapping or conflicting definitions; - meanings must be reused and governed across runs, teams, and agents; - the model or its context budget can't hold the full documentation; - users ask in business terms and need routing to the right source and grain. With one well-modeled source and a fixed set of questions, direct SQL may be enough. ## Quickstart This runs Auto Ontology with Docker Compose against Wide World Importers, Microsoft's sample sales database. You need Docker with Compose v2, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and an NVIDIA API key (`nvapi-...`) from [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com). 1. Clone the repository and create `.env`: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git && cd auto-ontology cp .env.example .env ``` Then set these values in `.env`: ```dotenv DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY=nvapi-... AUTH_SECRET= APP_URL=http://localhost:3000 POSTGRES_PASSWORD= CONNECTION_STRINGS=postgresql://postgres:@postgres:5432/wideworldimporters AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD= PGADMIN_PASSWORD= ``` Compose publishes Postgres, pgAdmin, and the web app on the host, so replace each default password before you start it. `.env.example` also sets an API key per model role: replace each `nvapi-your-api-key-here` with your key, or delete those lines so they fall back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_API_KEY`. 2. Start Postgres and load the sample database. The seed script lives in auto-ontology-eval; pass it the Postgres password you set: ```bash docker compose up -d --wait postgres git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval.git ../auto-ontology-eval (cd ../auto-ontology-eval && uv sync && cp .env.example .env && \ POSTGRES_PASSWORD='' \ uv run python scripts/seed/seed_wwi.py --database-name wideworldimporters --drop) ``` 3. Build and start the rest of the stack: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` 4. Open and sign in with `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_EMAIL` and `AUTO_ONTOLOGY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`. Go to **Settings → Semantic Compilation** and turn it on. Ingestion runs at startup; compilation starts immediately and reports **Semantic compilation is ready** when it finishes. 5. Ask a question in **Chat**: > What was revenue for the USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania > in June 2015? The agent resolves *revenue*, *product*, and *state* to terms in the ontology, follows their relationships to the joins it needs, and runs the query. The answer comes back with its SQL and the steps that produced it, so you can check the result against the source: ```text Answer: Revenue for USB food flash drive - sushi roll in Pennsylvania in June 2015 was $588.80, from 3 invoice lines. SQL: SELECT SUM(il.extendedprice) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS invoice_lines FROM sales.invoicelines il JOIN sales.invoices i ON il.invoiceid = i.invoiceid JOIN warehouse.stockitems si ON il.stockitemid = si.stockitemid JOIN sales.customers c ON i.customerid = c.customerid JOIN application.cities ct ON c.deliverycityid = ct.cityid JOIN application.stateprovinces sp ON ct.stateprovinceid = sp.stateprovinceid WHERE si.stockitemname = 'USB food flash drive - sushi roll' AND sp.stateprovincename = 'Pennsylvania' AND i.invoicedate >= '2015-06-01' AND i.invoicedate < '2015-07-01' Steps: Resolved terms: Invoice Line (revenue), Stock Item, State Province, Invoice Joined: invoice line -> invoice -> customer -> city -> state province Validated the filter values against the data, then executed ``` 6. Ask something the data can't answer. Wide World Importers has no advertising data, so a question about ad spend has nothing to resolve against. An agent connected through [MCP](#mcp-server) checks answerability first and asks you to clarify: ```text You: What was return on ad spend for the sushi roll flash drive in June 2015? Agent: check_answerable -> coverage 0.5; no term covers "ad spend" Agent: I can find revenue for that product, but this data has no advertising spend, so I can't compute return on ad spend. Do you want June 2015 revenue instead, or is ad spend tracked in another source I should connect? ``` If the UI loads without its left navigation after a restart, the browser is holding a stale session cookie. Clear site data for `localhost:3000` and sign in again. For other setup failures, see the [setup skill's troubleshooting guide](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/references/troubleshooting.md). ## How it works Auto Ontology works in two stages: it generates an ontology that people certify, and the agent answers questions from it. The ontology answers six questions, each with its own element: | Question | Element | In Auto Ontology | | ------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | What does it mean? | Concept | A term, such as *Customer* or *Invoice Line*, with a description and synonyms | | Where is it? | Mapping | Column attributes tie each term to the tables and columns that hold it | | What's connected? | Relationship | Joins between tables, including bridge tables: declared keys, plus inferred links confirmed against the data | | How do I calculate it? | Metric | SQL attributes: reviewed SQL under a term, such as a margin, reused so answers compute each measure the same way | | Where does it come from? | Lineage | Each term and attribute links to its source tables and columns, and each answer returns its SQL | | Should I use it? | Certification | Experts certify names, descriptions, and attributes, and certified elements are marked as reviewed | **Generate:** the ingestion service builds a first draft from the source databases, and people refine it. Semantic compilation starts once you turn it on in **Settings → Semantic Compilation**. - **Catalog ingest:** read tables, columns, keys, views, and query history; tag PII if you turn on PII detection; embed tables and columns in pgvector. - **Per table:** profile values with SQL. A model finds foreign key candidates and junction tables, writes column descriptions, and names the terms. - **Across tables:** group copies of a schema into term families, and link foreign keys to the terms they reference, keeping an inferred link only when the data confirms it. A model attaches foreign key columns left unlinked, suggests SQL attributes from query history and for bridge tables, and describes each column attribute. - **Output:** the ontology in Postgres with embeddings in pgvector, which you can import or export as Ossie YAML. - **Certify:** test the draft with real questions in Chat, or with `check_answerable` and `ask_question` over MCP. Refine terms, descriptions, and SQL attributes in the UI or through the API, and certify them once they're correct. Edits are re-embedded right away, and the next compilation keeps them, except which semantic foreign key each join uses, which every compilation re-selects. The [Generate tool flow](./docs/architecture.md#generate-an-ontology) shows which steps call a model and which are SQL or rules. The result is a semantic graph you can explore in the UI. In this example, one compilation of Wide World Importers produced 31 terms; selecting **Order** shows its description, related terms, mapped columns, and SQL attributes:

**Answer:** the reasoning model answers each question in a loop, choosing one tool at a time: - **`retrieve`:** search the semantic layer by meaning and by name for business concepts, column meanings, and named calculations. Results come back as tables and columns with their descriptions and stored values, definitions with their SQL, and join paths. The model searches again whenever something is missing. - **`run_sql`:** look at stored values or test a draft. Before the query runs, table and column names are checked against the catalog, and tables against what `retrieve` showed. - **`submit`:** give the final query and an explanation. The query is checked and run, and an error goes back to the model to fix. A question about the data itself, such as which tables exist or what a term means, is answered in words: `retrieve` looks it up with `purpose=information`, and `submit` returns the answer without SQL. - **Result:** the answer comes back with its SQL and the steps it took, and a chart in Chat. No tool calls a language model except `predict`, which answers predictive questions when `KUMO_RFM_API_URL` is set; see [Predictions](#predictions). If the model reaches its tool-call limit without an accepted query, the agent reports that the question can't be answered from this data. The [Answer tool flow](./docs/architecture.md#answer-a-question) shows the loop, its tools, and its limits. In Chat, each answer shows its SQL, and you can view the rows, download them as CSV, or read them as a chart:

Auto Ontology is compatible with [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/), the open standard for exchanging semantic models. Ossie includes a [converter for Auto Ontology](https://github.com/apache/ossie-converters/tree/main/nvidia), which Auto Ontology uses to import and export model definitions as Ossie YAML. Use **Settings → Import / Export**, or `POST /api/model/import` and `POST /api/model/export`. The services behind both stages, and how clients reach them: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph clients["Clients"] direction TB ui["Browser: web UI"] rest["Scripts: REST API with API tokens"] mcpc["MCP clients: Cursor, Claude Desktop, agents"] end mcp["MCP server: read-only tools (FastMCP, port 3003)"] fe["Web app, auth, API gateway (Next.js, port 3000)"] subgraph private["Private network"] direction TB be["Backend: text-to-SQL agent, catalog and ontology APIs (FastAPI, port 3001)"] ing["Ingestion and semantic compilation (FastAPI, port 3002)"] pg[("Postgres + pgvector: app data, catalog, ontology, embeddings")] end src[("Source databases: 10 connectors")] models["Model endpoints: NVIDIA NIM or OpenAI-compatible (reasoning, non-reasoning, embed, rerank)"] vault["Vault (optional): connection credentials"] kumo["KumoRFM (optional): predictions"] ui --> fe rest --> fe mcpc --> mcp mcp -- "public API" --> fe fe --> be fe -- "users, sessions, settings" --> pg be -- "trigger ingest and compile" --> ing be --> pg ing --> pg be -- "run SQL" --> src ing -- "read schema, sample values" --> src be --> models ing --> models be -.-> vault ing -.-> vault be -.-> kumo ``` | Component | Technology | Role | Port | | ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---- | | Frontend | Next.js, Better Auth, Prisma | Web UI for chat, catalog, analytics, and settings; auth and RBAC; public API gateway | 3000 | | Backend | FastAPI (Python 3.12+), LangChain | Text-to-SQL agent, catalog, ontology APIs | 3001 | | Ingestion service | FastAPI (Python 3.12+) | Ingestion and semantic compilation | 3002 | | MCP server | FastMCP | Read-only agent tools over the public API | 3003 | | Postgres + pgvector | PostgreSQL 17 | Catalog, ontology, app data, vector store | 5432 | | HashiCorp Vault | Optional | Connection credential storage | n/a | Browser and API clients go through the web app on port 3000, and MCP clients through the MCP server on port 3003, which calls the same public API. Keep ports 3001 and 3002 on a private network: FastAPI trusts the user identity the frontend forwards in the `x-auto-ontology-user-id` header, and the ingestion service's endpoints (ingest, delete, reset, compile) have no authentication of their own. Full pipeline detail, with tool-flow diagrams for generating an ontology and answering a question: [docs/architecture.md](./docs/architecture.md). ## Use it from your agent ### MCP server The [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server gives any MCP client read-only tools over the ontology. Each user signs in through Auto Ontology, and every call runs with that user's permissions. | Job | Tools | | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | Readiness | `check_readiness`: can this deployment answer anything at all | | Terms | `search_terms`, `get_term`, `get_term_columns`, `get_term_sql_attributes`, `get_sql_attribute`, `describe_table` | | Answerability | `check_answerable`: does the ontology cover this question | | Questions | `ask_question`: the answer, the SQL, and the rows | Run the server against your deployment: ```bash AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \ uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp ``` Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "url": "http://localhost:3003/mcp" } } } ``` Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), bridged with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote): ```json { "mcpServers": { "auto-ontology": { "command": "npx", "args": ["mcp-remote", "http://localhost:3003/mcp"] } } } ``` Restart the client after editing its config, then sign in when it prompts. Sign-in, configuration, and troubleshooting are in [docs/mcp.md](./docs/mcp.md). ### Agent skills Three skills teach a coding agent to work with Auto Ontology. Start at [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md). | Skill | Covers | | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | [`nvidia-ontology-setup`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-setup/) | Install, connect sources, compile, prove readiness | | [`nvidia-ontology-management`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-management/) | Inspect, model, certify, import/export, and publish | | [`nvidia-ontology-query`](./skills/nvidia-ontology-query/) | Ask questions and validate the SQL, rows, and answer | ### REST API Ask a question with `POST /api/chat/completions` on the web app's origin. Mint an API token under the user menu → **API Tokens**. The response is a server-sent event stream: a `result` event carries the answer, and `data: [DONE]` ends the stream. ```bash curl -N http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions \ -H "x-api-key: $AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}' ``` ```python import json import os import requests response = requests.post( "http://localhost:3000/api/chat/completions", headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["AUTO_ONTOLOGY_API_TOKEN"]}, json={"question": "How many orders shipped last week?"}, stream=True, timeout=900, ) response.raise_for_status() for line in response.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True): if not line or not line.startswith("data:"): continue payload = line.removeprefix("data:").strip() if payload == "[DONE]": break event = json.loads(payload) if event["type"] == "result": print(event["answer"]["response"]) print(event["answer"]["sql_code"]) elif event["type"] == "error": raise RuntimeError(event["message"]) ``` Event types, multi-turn conversations, and the gateway trust boundary are in [docs/conversation-api.md](./docs/conversation-api.md). Every other operation is in the [OpenAPI spec](./docs/openapi/auto-ontology-api.json). ## Connectors, models, and predictions ### Sources Auto Ontology connects to ten engines: - PostgreSQL - MySQL - Databricks - Snowflake - ClickHouse - Trino - Apache Kyuubi - HeavyDB - DuckDB - SQLite Add connections under **Settings → Connections**, or list them in `CONNECTION_STRINGS`. DuckDB and SQLite are connection-string only. See [docs/connections.md](./docs/connections.md) for URL schemes, scoping, and credential storage. ### Models Auto Ontology uses four model roles. With an `nvapi-` key, each defaults to an NVIDIA NIM on [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com): | Role | Default model | What it does | | --------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `REASONING` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` | Runs the answering agent and `check_answerable`, builds the ontology, and detects PII | | `NON_REASONING` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning-30b-a3b` | Rewrites follow-up questions, plans charts, writes PQL for predictions, and runs the quick steps of interactive analysis | | `EMBED` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-embed-1b` | Indexes tables, columns, terms, and SQL attributes in pgvector, and matches each question to them | | `RERANK` | `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-rerank-8b` | Picks the term that owns each bridge-table SQL attribute during compilation; not used to answer questions | To use self-hosted NIM or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set `_ENDPOINT`, `_API_KEY`, and `_MODEL`. Any field you leave unset falls back to `DEFAULT_MODELS_`, so the simplest setup fills in `DEFAULT_MODELS_*` and overrides only what differs; `*_API_KEY` also falls back to the legacy `NVIDIA_API_KEY`. Use models that support structured output, and keep the embedding model the same for ingestion and queries. [`.env.example`](./.env.example) documents every variable. ### Predictions Set `KUMO_RFM_API_URL` (and `KUMO_RFM_API_KEY` if your endpoint requires one) and the agent routes predictive questions to KumoRFM. KumoRFM is a hosted service: to answer, the agent uploads the connected tables to it, capped by `KUMO_MAX_TABLES` (20 by default) and `KUMO_MAX_ROWS_PER_TABLE` (unlimited unless set). Review what that sends, and complete your organization's data review, before you enable it. ## Benchmarks To run a text-to-SQL benchmark such as BIRD, refer to [auto-ontology-eval](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology-eval), which scores the same model with and without the ontology on [NeMo Gym](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym). ## Contributing We welcome contributions: bug fixes, connectors, documentation, and examples. Please read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting pull requests.
